plugins.name: nerf-receipts
plugins.description: A personal flight recorder for Claude Code quality: records your own per-session failure rate, edit churn, and tokens/task by model version, and flags real shifts when a model changes.

plugins.name: dead-rules-audit
plugins.description: CLAUDE.md compliance scorecard: tallies which rules Claude actually follows vs ignores as you edit, and flags chronically-ignored rules to promote into a deterministic hook.

plugins.name: pr-provenance-stamp
plugins.description: Stamps a provenance receipt (prompts, estimated spend, tests run with exit codes, and a truthful agent-authored line split) into your PR body on `gh pr create`.

plugins.name: standup-autopilot
plugins.description: Writes your daily standup from what your agents actually did across repos: captures tasks, tests, PRs, and blockers from session transcripts and re-injects yesterday's open blockers next session.

plugins.name: dead-end-registry
plugins.description: Remembers approaches you tried and reverted (with reason and estimated token cost) and warns before you retry them, via a prompt-submit card and an ask-before-edit guard.

plugins.name: bounty-board
plugins.description: Prices your repo's TODO/FIXME/HACK debt as aging XP bounties, injects the top 3 as opportunistic side quests, and verifies + pays out bounties you genuinely clear.

plugins.name: block-dangerous-commands
plugins.description: PreToolUse guard for Bash: blocks dangerous shell commands (rm -rf ~, fork bombs, curl|sh, force push to main) before they run, with three safety levels and opt-in per-level ask mode.

plugins.name: protect-secrets
plugins.description: Secrets firewall for tool calls: denies (or asks, per level) any Read/Edit/Write/Bash that would read, modify, or exfiltrate .env files, SSH keys, cloud credentials, or keystores, with tiered safety levels tunable via HOOK_SAFETY_LEVEL.

plugins.name: git-safety
plugins.description: Branch-aware git guardrails plus destructive gh CLI protection: denies pushes to main/master, protected-branch deletion, direct commit/merge/rebase/reset/push on a protected branch, and gh pr merge/close, issue close, release and repo delete.

plugins.name: protect-tests
plugins.description: Stops "fake green" test-gaming: blocks the agent from deleting, renaming-away, or skip/xfail-disabling tests so it fixes the code instead, across pytest, jest, Go, JUnit, RSpec, and more.

plugins.name: case-insensitive-guard
plugins.description: Stops `rm -rf content` destroying `Content` on case-insensitive filesystems (APFS/exFAT/NTFS): resolves the real target of destructive commands through cd chains, quotes, and subshells, and denies provable case collisions.

plugins.name: config-guard
plugins.description: Who guards the guards: blocks the agent from tampering with its own guardrail config (settings.json, hook scripts, hooks.json, .mcp.json, plugin manifests, claude CLI config writes); reads always pass.

plugins.name: config-watch
plugins.description: Tripwire for out-of-band config changes: warns on every mid-session settings/skills change (or blocks it with CONFIG_WATCH_BLOCK=true) to catch installer scripts and npm payloads rewriting settings behind Claude Code's back.

plugins.name: auto-stage
plugins.description: Automatic git staging: runs `git add` on every file Claude edits or writes, so `git status` always shows exactly what Claude touched and pre-commit review needs no manual staging.

plugins.name: format-code
plugins.description: Auto-formats files the moment Claude writes them: ruff for Python, prettier for JS/TS/JSON/MD/YAML/HTML, with shell-injection-safe argv execution and silent skips for everything else.

plugins.name: session-logger
plugins.description: Durable markdown log of every session (cwd, git repo, files touched, secret-redacted bash commands), appended async so logging never blocks Claude.

plugins.name: instructions-audit
plugins.description: Prompt-injection tripwire for CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules files: flags invisible-Unicode smuggling, secret read/exfil directives, curl|sh, decode-and-execute, and hook/settings tampering as instructions load, then locks the session (every prompt and tool call denied) until a human clears it.

plugins.name: notify-permission
plugins.description: Slack alerts when Claude Code needs you: posts a rich card (project, session, and what needs approval) to your webhook on permission, idle, and choice prompts.

plugins.name: guard-pack
plugins.description: All six guard hooks in one Node process: config-guard, block-dangerous-commands, protect-secrets, protect-tests, git-safety, and case-insensitive-guard, first blocking verdict wins. One ~35 ms Node startup per tool call instead of six. Do not install alongside the individual guard plugins.

name: antigravity
description: Claude Code plugin: run the Antigravity CLI (Gemini) as a collaborating sub-agent with intelligent model routing across the SDLC. Community project; not affiliated with Google/Anthropic.

manifest.name: antigravity
manifest.description: Run the Antigravity CLI (Gemini) as a collaborating AI inside Claude Code, with intelligent model routing across the SDLC. Claude conducts — requirements, architecture, the hard 20%, verification, review — and routes deterministic, high-volume work (scaffolding, tests, first-pass review, migrations, web/Vertex AI Search) to Antigravity. Hybrid agentic engineering; lower token cost as a financial lever.

default_tier.title: Default Antigravity tier
default_tier.description: Tier used by agy-delegate.sh when --tier is not passed. One of: flash (Gemini 3.7 Flash High, default — bulk work), flash-lo (Flash Low, cheapest/trivial), pro (Gemini 3.1 Pro High, harder reasoning).

timeout.title: Default delegation timeout
timeout.description: Default agy print-mode timeout when --timeout is not passed, e.g. 5m, 10m, 300s.

coding_policy.title: Inject routing policy at session start
coding_policy.description: When on, a SessionStart hook injects this plugin's cost-aware routing policy (delegate above the break-even, keep Claude's context lean, always verify agy's output) as session context, so the discipline applies without invoking the skill. Set to off/false/0/no to suppress.

default_model.title: Default executor model (exact agy model name)
default_model.description: agy is multi-model. Set an exact model name from `agy models` (e.g. a Claude/GPT model on plans that expose them) to use as the executor when --tier/--model are not passed. Leave empty to use the tier mapping (Gemini by default). The 'Claude conducts, a different/cheaper model executes' design gives the cost + cross-model-verification benefit, so a non-Claude executor is recommended.

tier_flash.title: Model for the 'flash' tier
tier_flash.description: Override the exact agy model the 'flash' tier maps to (default: Gemini 3.7 Flash (High)). Use a name from `agy models`.

tier_flash_lo.title: Model for the 'flash-lo' tier
tier_flash_lo.description: Override the exact agy model the 'flash-lo' tier maps to (default: Gemini 3.7 Flash (Low)). Use a name from `agy models`.

tier_pro.title: Model for the 'pro' tier
tier_pro.description: Override the exact agy model the 'pro' tier maps to (default: Gemini 3.1 Pro (High)). Use a name from `agy models`.

structured_output.title: Use agy's structured JSON output
structured_output.description: When on (default), agy-delegate runs agy with --output-format json (agy >= 1.1.8, requires python3) to classify failures from the structured error and report token usage as an AGY_USAGE line on stderr. The text on stdout is unchanged. Set to off/false/0/no to force the plain-text path.

digest_warn_chars.title: Digest-size warning threshold (chars)
digest_warn_chars.description: agy-delegate warns on stderr when a reply exceeds this many characters — a raw dump instead of the digest the cost discipline calls for. Empty = 8000. Set 0 to disable.

delegation_nudge.title: Nudge delegation on bulk-looking prompts
delegation_nudge.description: When on, a UserPromptSubmit hook adds a short advisory note to Claude's context when a prompt looks like bulk work above the delegation break-even (mass edits, migrations, exhaustive tests, fan-out search). Advisory only — Claude still makes the break-even judgment per task. Set to off/false/0/no to suppress.

usage_log.title: Cost-measurement log file (AGY_USAGE / AGY_SIGNAL)
usage_log.description: Absolute path. When set, every delegation appends its AGY_USAGE (token counts) and AGY_SIGNAL (failure) line to this file in addition to stderr. Use this whenever you are MEASURING cost: stderr is easily lost — piping the wrapper through `2>&1 | tail -N` to keep Claude's context lean keeps the digest and silently drops the usage line, which makes the Gemini side look cheaper than it is. Env AGY_USAGE_LOG overrides this. Empty = off.

plugins.name: han
plugins.description: Meta-plugin that installs the bundled Han suite. Has no components of its own; it depends on han-communication, han-core, han-documentation, han-research, han-planning, han-coding, han-github, and han-reporting so installing it pulls them all in. Does not bundle the opt-in han-feedback, han-atlassian, or han-plugin-builder plugins.

plugins.name: han-communication
plugins.description: Foundational communication plugin for the Han suite. Owns the canonical readability standard, writing-voice profile, and explanation standard, the readability-guidance skill that surfaces the first two into a calling skill's context for in-voice drafting, the explanation-guidance skill that surfaces the third at the point a run talks to a person, the readability-editor agent that runs the adversarial rewrite, and the edit-for-readability skill. Depends on nothing and sits beneath every other plugin; the plugins that produce prose output depend on it.

plugins.name: han-core
plugins.description: The shared foundation of the Han suite: the specialist agent roster the other plugins dispatch, the project-discovery skill with its project-scanner agent, and the canonical evidence and YAGNI rule files. The documentation skills live in han-documentation, the pre-planning research skills in han-research, the planning skills in han-planning, and the coding skills in han-coding; each depends on han-core.

plugins.name: han-documentation
plugins.description: Documentation skills for the Han suite: writing down what the team built and decided. Home of project-documentation, architectural-decision-record, and runbook. Depends on han-communication and han-core; bundled by the han meta-plugin.

plugins.name: han-research
plugins.description: Pre-planning knowledge-work skills for the Han suite: understanding a problem before anyone commits to a plan. Home of research, gap-analysis, and issue-triage, plus the research-analyst agent. Depends on han-communication and han-core; bundled by the han meta-plugin.

plugins.name: han-planning
plugins.description: Planning skills for the Han suite: specifying, planning, sequencing, breaking down, and stress-testing work before implementation. Home of plan-a-feature, plan-implementation, plan-a-phased-build, plan-work-items, and iterative-plan-review, plus the discussion-facilitator agent. Depends on han-communication and han-core; bundled by the han meta-plugin.

plugins.name: han-coding
plugins.description: Code-writing and execution skills for the Han suite. Home of the tdd skill, which drives a feature or behavior through a BDD-framed red-green-refactor loop with an enforced observed-failure gate. Depends on han-core and han-communication; bundled by the han meta-plugin.

plugins.name: han-github
plugins.description: GitHub-specific extensions to Han. Provides skills to post code reviews as PR comments, update a PR description with a consistent format, and other GitHub-facing workflows.

plugins.name: han-reporting
plugins.description: Reporting and summary skills for the Han suite. Turns feature specifications into plain-language stakeholder summaries (also called executive or business summaries) with diagrams, for sharing with non-technical stakeholders before implementation kicks off.

plugins.name: han-feedback
plugins.description: Post-session feedback skill for the Han suite. Captures structured observations, ratings, and improvement ideas on the Han skills you ran in a session and optionally posts them as a GitHub issue to testdouble/han. Opt-in: installed on its own, not pulled in by the han meta-plugin.

plugins.name: han-atlassian
plugins.description: Atlassian-facing extensions to the Han suite. Adds markdown-to-confluence, which publishes a local Markdown file to a user-specified Confluence page; project-documentation-to-confluence, which runs the han-documentation project-documentation skill and then publishes the result there; investigate-to-confluence, which runs the core investigate skill and publishes the resulting investigation report there; code-overview-to-confluence, which runs the core code-overview skill and publishes the resulting overview there; plan-a-feature-to-confluence, which runs the core plan-a-feature skill and publishes the spec and its companion artifacts there as a page tree; and work-items-to-jira, which creates one Jira ticket per slice from a work-items file. All work through the Atlassian MCP server. Depends on han-core, han-documentation, han-planning, and han-coding (its wrapper skills run skills from each and its wrapped skills dispatch the shared han-core agents), and on han-communication (its wrapped prose-producing skills source the shared readability standard), and requires a configured Atlassian MCP server. Opt-in: installed on its own, not pulled in by the han meta-plugin.

plugins.name: han-linear
plugins.description: Linear-facing extensions to the Han suite. Adds work-items-to-linear, which creates one Linear issue per slice from a work-items file. Works through the Linear MCP server and requires it to be configured. Depends on no other Han plugin. Opt-in: installed on its own, not pulled in by the han meta-plugin.

plugins.name: han-plugin-builder
plugins.description: Guidance for building Claude Code skills, agents, and plugins. The guidance skill answers authoring questions and, run with init, vendors the full guidance set into a repo as a path-scoped rule index so the right guidance surfaces while editing skill and agent files. Opt-in and dependency-free: installed on its own, not pulled in by the han meta-plugin.

name: sloptrim
description: A local detector for AI-writing patterns. Scores every prose file your agent saves. Python standard library only, no network, no model.

manifest.name: sloptrim
manifest.description: Scores the first 256 KB of extracted prose from files accepted up to 512 KB for plain text and 4 MB for supported archives, against a catalogue of 71 documented patterns, 62 of them with a detector behind them and 50 able to move the score. It names the ones that fired so the flagged spans get fixed before the file ships. The 0 to 100 score lands in one of five bands: clean, light tells, mixed, heavy tells, pervasive tells. Every band describes the prose and none of them names an author. Reads 20 formats including .docx and .epub. Deterministic, Python standard library only, no network, no model. Prose only; code, config and commits stay untouched.

hooks.command: node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/sloptrim-activate.js"
node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/sloptrim-subagent.js"

node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/sloptrim-guard.js"

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.endpoint_probe: POST tools/list on https://analyticslegends.ai/mcp -> 200, 20 tools, protocol 2025-11-25, 3 resources, 4 prompts. Paid conformance 2026-08-18 on the deployed fingerprint: 686 assertions, 0 failed.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.long_description: Curated, source-backed intelligence on the SAP analytics services market (Datasphere, Business Data Cloud, SAP Analytics Cloud, BW/4HANA, Databricks), read-only, so an assistant can answer precisely and cite the exact record. TWENTY tools: FOURTEEN public and unauthenticated, plus SIX a subscriber key opens (listed, refusing by name, never hidden): a directory of SAP consulting, recruitment and vendor organisations searchable by country and kind, a profile per firm, and an aggregate count for an agent that needs a number, not a page of rows; a published day-rate aggregate by geography, stack and seniority — small, all secondary sources, sample_size null where no observation matches the cell, GBP/CHF never folded into euro rows; a live contract radar of publicly published SAP analytics openings, each with its own page — filter it by employment_type, because it is mostly PERMANENT roles and an unfiltered page answers a contracting question with salaried jobs; many rows carry a panel-inferred P25-P75 day-rate band for their seniority x product x region cell, served with its basis, sample and source so it is never quotable as the employer's own offer; what is gated there is a FIELD, not a row: the verified link to the original listing is the Consultant deliverable, every other fact and the page stay public; a curated market-news corpus de-duplicated by upstream URL, its size read at query time and returned as _meta.match_count, each item carrying the upstream publisher's URL alongside ours; a concept encyclopaedia of the stack's vocabulary; the SAP module lookup; and the metadata of the deep-research studies on market structure, day rates and recruiter economics — each exists in EN and FR, so the tool returns EDITIONS and counting rows double-counts studies. Also public: the CV/profile platforms a consultant can sign up on, the Academy catalogue, and a traversal of the learning knowledge graph. Every tool is annotated readOnlyHint. The fourteen public tools need no credential; the six paid ones need an analyticslegends.ai subscription (Consultant or above) or the MCP Pass (€39.90/month, analyticslegends.ai/pricing) — three open at Consultant (the full concept card, a study body, an Academy module) and three at Legend (firm intelligence, and the SAP end-customer corpus with its per-customer profile). A key on a FREE account gets a small daily taste of the paid tranche (the number is in analytics-legends://tranche). Retrieval with attribution is permitted, training is not; every response carries a citation_url. DELIBERATELY NOT SERVED at any tier: the opportunity-to-consultant matchers, and people — consultants are held as initials only; no tool returns anyone's identity or contact details.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.monitoring: Handshake, a real tools/call with data, and latency. Two watchers: a 20-minute tick on the maintainer's workstation (only while awake), and a cloud backstop twice a day calling tools/list AND a data-returning tools/call (added 2026-08-18; before that it watched the website only). Health: https://analyticslegends.ai/api/mcp-health.json — read its generated_at, do not assume a cadence.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.repository_scope: This repository is the server's PUBLIC FACE — manifest, descriptor, client config, docs. It carries no server code (the application repository is private: paid corpus, personal data). tools/list against the endpoint is the authority for the surface.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.tools_served: 20 on this endpoint: 14 public and unauthenticated, 6 gated by tier and refused by name (3 at Consultant, 3 at Legend). The MCP Pass opens all six.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.transport_path: Cloudflare Worker on analyticslegends.ai/mcp* -> Supabase Edge Function -> Postgres
